newsitem.title: USA: U.S. nonfinancial debt rise moderated in Q3.
newsitem.headline: U.S. nonfinancial debt rise moderated in Q3.

text.p: Total debt held by U.S. households; businesses; and federal, state and local governments grew at a seasonally adjusted 4.7 percent annual rate in the third quarter, the Federal Reserve said Wednesday.
That was down from a 4.9 percent rate of increase in the second quarter and a 6.3 percent rate in the first quarter.
Nonfinancial debt represents borrowings by all economic sectors except banks, thrifts, finance companies and other financial services providers.
Federal government debt picked up to a 4.3 percent annual rate of increase in the third quarter from 1.7 percent in the second quarter.

But the Fed said debts of nonfederal sectors -- households, business and state and local governments -- slowed to a 4.8 percent rate of rise from 6.1 percent in the second quarter. The rate of increase in household debts kept falling to a 6.3 percent rate from 7.7 percent in the second quarter and 9.2 percent in the first three months this year.
Both home mortgage and consumer credit borrowing slowed, the Fed said.
Business debt grew at a 6.0 percent rate in the third quarter, up from 4.8 percent in the second quarter.
"Business borrowing at banks was particularly robust and net issuance of corporate bonds remained brisk," the Fed said.

Debts of state and local governments ran down at a 7.1 percent annual rate in the third quarter after growing at a 2.8 percent rate in the second quarter. "Retirements of previously refunded debt were particularly large in the third quarter and outpaced new issuance by a wide margin," the Fed said.

At the end of the third quarter, total domestic nonfinancial debt outstanding was $14.4 trillion -- including $3.8 trillion owed by the federal government and about $10.7 trillion owed by nonfederal sectors.
